items.t: Said that books in the Chapel Hill-Carrboro school district are not in compliance with the state Parents' Bill of Rights law.
items.q: North Carolina State Rep. Brenden Jones grills Chapel Hill-Carrboro school district officials on books he says aren't in compliance with Parents' Bill of Rights state law.

record.t: Was the lead primary sponsor of the original HB 283.
record.q: Rep. Brenden Jones, who represents the 46th District in Columbus and Robeson counties, was the lead primary sponsor of the original HB 283.

record.t: Filed HB1043, the CHCCS Act, which would close some loopholes identified in a hearing, clarify legislative intent, and cut central office funding for willfully noncompliant school districts.
record.q: Jones closed by announcing that he had filed HB1043—the CHCCS Act (for Curriculum, Honesty, Compliance, and Child Safety) which would close some of the loopholes identified in the hearing, clarify legislative intent, and cut central office funding for willfully noncompliant school districts.

record.t: Served as co-chair of the House Select Committee on Disaster Relief.
record.q: the Co-Chairs of the House Select Committee on Disaster Relief John Bell and Brenden Jones

record.t: Displayed a photo of a page from "Grandad's Pride" at a hearing on Chapel Hill-Carrboro schools' library books.
record.q: Jones displayed a photo of a page from “Grandad’s Pride” by Harry Woodgate and read a passage from “It Feels Good to Be Yourself: A Book About Gender Identity”
